newsitem.title: USA: Trump seeks sale of A.C. casino.
newsitem.headline: Trump seeks sale of A.C. casino.

text.p: Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc has retained an advisor and is "aggresively pursuing" the sale of one of its three casino-hotels in Atlantic City, company president Nicholas Ribis said.

"We've retained Merrill Lynch to pursue the disposition of one of our Atlantic City casinos," Ribis said in a telephone interview. He did not specify which of the three Atlantic City casinos operated by the company would be sold.

Explaining the purpose of a sale, Ribis said, "We think the market place in Atlantic City is strong. There is a lot of interest in Atlantic City by a number of companies, and we think that the price that the property we're attempting to sell will fetch will be substantial."
"(It will) give the company an opportunity to diversify and reduce some of its debt," he said.
The proceeds "could" fund a new project by the company somewhere, Ribis said, but he declined to be more specific.
Asked about a timetable for a sale, Ribis said, "The timetable is, we're aggressively pursuing it."

The Atlantic City market faces increased competition in the future, with Trump rivals led by Mirage Resorts Inc planning new casino projects in the city's marina district. Donald Trump, who controls Trump Hotels, has opposed plans by the state of New Jersey to pay much of the cost of a road and tunnel project to serve the area, where he already operates a recently renovated casino -- the former Trump Castle, now known as the Trump Marina.
Donald Trump in June announced he intended to apply for a casino license in Detroit, after that city appoved legalized gambling last year.
